# Mission by Managed Code

> An open-source patronage initiative where companies fund a team of maintainers to keep the open-source dependencies they rely on healthy — with reserved maintainer capacity and real SLAs — while training juniors in the open.

## What Mission is

Mission is run by Managed Code as a modern take on Renaissance patronage for the digital commons. Instead of one-off, anonymous donations, patron companies retain a team of maintainers who keep their critical open-source dependencies maintained, secure, and up to date. There is no fixed sticker price: a patron funds a maintainer at a developer GRADE — roughly that grade's payroll — and each grade reserves a scoped capacity band plus a first-response SLA. Junior developers learn the craft in the open by working alongside the team on real upstream issues.

## Funding goal

Mission launches when monthly patronage covers a working team: **$32,768 a month** (2¹⁵ — a wink to the developers reading). **$6k a month** is committed so far, about **18%** of the way there. (Illustrative while Mission is in launch.)

## Patron grades (no fixed price — salary-grade retainers, not hour packs)

- **Trainee** — ~4–6 focused maintainer-hours per month, 72-hour first human response, 1 dependency watched and triaged (senior-reviewed). Roughly trainee-grade payroll.
- **Junior** — ~10–15 focused maintainer-hours per month, 24-hour first human response, up to 2 dependencies watched. Roughly junior-grade payroll.
- **Mid** (recommended) — ~25–40 focused maintainer-hours per month, 8-business-hour first response, up to 3 dependencies adopted, a named maintainer. Roughly mid-level payroll.
- **Senior** — ~45–60 focused maintainer-hours per month, 4-business-hour critical response, up to 5 dependencies plus backport planning, a named senior + private channel, and mentorship budget. Roughly senior-grade payroll.

Billed monthly. Capacity bands are planning ranges, not billable-hour packs. Response windows and figures are set in each patronage agreement and are illustrative while Mission is in launch.

## Who runs it

Managed Code — a .NET open-source community. We build and maintain open-source libraries and tools in the open.

- GitHub: https://github.com/managedcode
- Made in Ukraine.
- Contact: opensource@managed-code.com

## Key facts

- 98% of codebases contain open-source components.
- Fewer than 40% of GitHub Sponsors profiles ever receive a donation.
- The average organization spends roughly $670k per year on workarounds for fixes that never land upstream.

Learn more: https://mission.managed-code.com
